strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing asymmetric alignment between single visual and hierarchical textual features with clear problem formulation
Solid heterogeneous manifold alignment algorithm with theoretical guarantees (existence and uniqueness of optimal intermediate manifold)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four datasets, multiple protocols (few-shot, base-to-base/novel/whole), and three complementary metrics
Consistent improvements across settings, especially on HCA metric (up to 28.83% improvement in 16-shot, 41.17% vs HyCoCLIP)
Effective visualizations (attention maps, t-SNE) and thorough ablation studies validating each component
Strong reproducibility efforts with detailed implementation, complete proofs, and commitment to open-source release
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components (intermediate layers, cross-attention, hyperbolic embeddings all established); main contribution (heterogeneous curvatures) is incremental

Theoretical contributions somewhat expected: Theorem 1 relies on Taylor approximation without discussing approximation error bounds or validity conditions; Propositions 1-2 provide intuitive but not surprising guarantees
Key hyperparameter choices lack justification: Why layers 4 and 7? No ablation on layer selection; k=0.1 in cone formula fixed without sensitivity analysis; α=0.5 for entailment loss not validated

Missing statistical rigor: results averaged over only 3 runs with no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; modest improvements in some settings (1-3%) don't clearly justify added complexity

Insufficient experimental scope: limited baseline comparisons, evaluation restricted to hierarchical classification, unclear applicability to other hierarchical VLM tasks (retrieval, detection, segmentation)
External hierarchy dependency not addressed: for CIFAR-100/SUN/ImageNet, hierarchies constructed from WordNet may not reflect actual image distributions; Rare Species performance notably weaker

Method complexity insufficiently justified: combines many components (intermediate layers, cross-attention, dual hyperbolic spaces, intermediate manifold search via golden section + implicit differentiation, entailment constraints); computational overhead vs baselines not reported

Design decisions lack validation: motivation for intermediate manifold alignment versus direct alignment unclear; cross-attention mechanism is standard without comparing alternatives; entailment constraints not validated as optimal for hierarchical relationships

strengths: Well-motivated asymmetry problem in modality alignment with clear intuition
Solid theoretical contributions with rigorous proofs (Theorems 1 and Propositions 1-2)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, settings (few-shot, base-to-novel, etc.), and metrics
Consistent improvements across all evaluation protocols, with notable gains in hierarchical metrics (28.83% HCA improvement)
Strong visualization and interpretability analysis (T-SNE, GradCAM attention maps) demonstrating learned hierarchical features
Detailed ablation studies validating each component's contribution
Good reproducibility effort with extensive appendices and promise of code release
weaknesses: Taylor approximation in Theorem 1 lacks rigor—no error bounds provided for the approximation quality
Core assumption about heterogeneous manifolds is not empirically validated—actual learned curvature values not analyzed or visualized
Marginal gains from heterogeneous manifolds (HypV1 to full method often <1%), undermining the central motivation
Key design choices poorly justified: disabling cross-token self-attention, selecting layers 4&7 for intermediate features, fixed δ parameter—lack empirical validation
No statistical significance testing despite modest improvements in many settings (1-3%); results averaged over only 3 runs without error bars
Limited baseline comparisons—hyperbolic methods only in one table; main comparisons are with MaPLe/PromptSRC variants
Computational cost and complexity not analyzed; practical implementation details missing (golden section search tolerance, gradient computation numerics)
Evaluation scope narrow—limited to TOS classification tasks; generalization to other hierarchical vision-language problems unclear
Novelty is incremental—primarily combines existing techniques (cross-attention, hyperbolic embeddings, entailment cones) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates the asymmetry in existing methods and proposes an intuitive hierarchical alignment solution
Solid theoretical contributions: Theorems 1-2 and Propositions 1-2 provide formal guarantees for intermediate manifold construction, even if based on approximations
Comprehensive experimental validation: extensive experiments across 4 datasets, 3 metrics, multiple settings with consistent improvements and thorough ablations
Strong technical execution: semantic-aware feature extraction framework is well-designed; use of learnable curvatures per modality is sensible
Excellent reproducibility: complete proofs, implementation details, hyperparameters, and visualizations; commitment to open-source release
Effective qualitative analysis: GradCAM visualizations convincingly demonstrate hierarchical attention patterns align with taxonomic levels
weaknesses: Theoretical approximations weaken guarantees: Taylor expansion introduces 5.3% mean error; distance measure D_L is not a formal metric (asymmetric, violates triangle inequality); constant r estimation is ad-hoc
Limited component-level novelty: intermediate layers, hyperbolic embeddings, and cross-attention are all established techniques; the contribution is primarily in their combination
Narrow scope: method is specialized for hierarchical/taxonomic data; applicability to standard vision-language tasks without hierarchies is unclear and unexplored

Mixed experimental results: performance gains vary significantly by dataset—strongest on naturally hierarchical data (CIFAR100, Rare Species) but weaker on artificial hierarchies (ImageNet, SUN); base-to-novel generalization shows inconsistent transfer

Methodological concerns: cross-token attention suppression lacks strong empirical grounding; layer selection (4,7,11) justification via Information Bottleneck is hand-wavy; claimed 'symmetric alignment' still enforces asymmetric entailment constraints
Incomplete comparisons: missing direct comparisons with hierarchical VLM methods (BioCLIP, BioCLIP2); only two hyperbolic baselines; no comparisons with other intermediate-layer fusion approaches
Presentation issues: paper is dense with heavy notation; frequent appendix references make standalone reading difficult; complexity may limit accessibility
Practical overhead: ~30% training time increase and multiple hyperparameters add complexity for prompt-tuning applications; sensitivity to hierarchy quality/definition not thoroughly analyzed
